department: Department of Marine and Environmental Sciences (Halmos College of Arts and Sciences)

deadline.value: Rolling admissions for August (Fall), May (Summer), and January (Winter) starts (prior-cycle Fall deadline was July 17; international on-site applicants are advised to complete applications 4 months before the term starts).
deadline.quote: Admissions is on a “rolling” basis with program start dates offered in August (Fall term), May (Summer term) and January (Winter term).

also.quote: International applicants wishing to study on-site should complete their application 4 months before the start of the term.

gre_subject.value: ETS offers no GRE Subject Test in Oceanography/Marine Biology (Subject Tests exist only in Mathematics, Physics, and Psychology).
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Applicants must secure a major adviser in the Department of Marine and Environmental Sciences before applying and submit their NSU Faculty Letter of Endorsement detailing the lab and 3+ years of funding.
supervisor.quote: Letter of Endorsement from an NSU faculty member. Note: The NSU Faculty Letter of endorsement is the most important item for the application. ... Without that letter, NSU cannot review your application.

also.quote: The Ph.D. in Marine Biology/Oceanography does require that you find a major adviser prior to entrance into the doctoral program.

funding.value: Scholarships, GA/TA/RA positions (doctoral GA stipend up to $15,600/yr; RA typically includes 50%-80% tuition waiver plus hourly pay) are competitive and not guaranteed; the major adviser's endorsement letter must detail 3+ years of funding.
funding.quote: There are opportunities for financial support for your graduate work in the form of scholarships and jobs within the University. The scholarships and employment opportunities are highly competitive and are not guaranteed.

also.quote: The major adviser needs to write a detailed letter of support, explaining that they will serve as your major adviser and how you will receive at least three years of funding to support your studies.
Halmos College Graduate Assistantship for Doctoral Students Award Amount: Stipend up to a maximum of $15,600 per year, paid bi-weekly

entry_route.value: A master's degree is required to apply (minimum 3.50 master's GPA; 3.00 major / 2.90 cumulative bachelor's GPA).
entry_route.quote: A master's degree is required in order to apply, and is preferred to be in Biological Oceanography, Biology, Marine Biology, or another related science.

app_fee.value: Requires the NSU graduate application with a $50 USD application fee.

gre_general.value: GRE General scores (taken within the past 5 years) are required for the Ph.D. in Oceanography/Marine Biology.
gre_general.quote: Submit GRE scores (taken within the past 5 years).

also.quote: The Ph.D. in Oceanography/Marine Biology is the only exception and will still require the GRE for admission.

toefl_min.value: Minimum TOEFL iBT score is 80+ on the old scale (or 4+ on the new scale); HCAS also lists IELTS and PTE Academic without publishing a numeric IELTS minimum.
toefl_min.quote: Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) official iBT score of 80+ (old test scale) or 4+ (new test scale).

english_waiver.value: Exempt only for graduates of an approved U.S. institution where English is the primary language of instruction; graduates of foreign institutions (including India) must submit English test scores.
english_waiver.quote: Non-native English speakers and graduates of Foreign Institutions (where English is not the primary language instruction) must demonstrate English-language proficiency through one of the following options: Successful completion of a degree at an approved U.S. institution of higher education where English is the primary language of instruction. Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) official iBT score of 80+ (old test scale) or 4+ (new test scale).

notes: Covers Marine Biology and Physical Oceanography tracks at NSU Oceanographic Campus (Dania Beach, FL); minimum 76 credits beyond the baccalaureate (up to 30 graduate transfer credits possible).
name: Ph.D. in Marine Biology/Oceanography
